description: multiplication and division bind tighter than + and -
** is right associative
+ concatenates once either side is a string, left to right
template literal interpolates expressions
program: const n = 3; `n=${n + 1}!`

description: template literals nest
interpolated values are stringified like String()
program: `${null} ${undefined} ${[1, 2]} ${true} ${1.5}`

description: let reassignment and compound assignment operators
assigning to a const is a runtime error on that line
program:
const c = 1
c = 2

description: calling an undeclared name fails the run
program: nope()

description: == coerces, === does not, NaN is never equal to itself
program: [1 == "1", 1 === "1", null == undefined, null === undefined, NaN === NaN, 0 == "", "a" != "b", 1 !== 1]

description: typeof covers every value kind and undeclared names
program: [typeof 1, typeof "s", typeof true, typeof null, typeof undefined, typeof nope, typeof (() => 1), typeof [], typeof {}]

description: falsy values are 0 empty-string null undefined NaN false; everything else is truthy
?? only replaces null/undefined; || and && use truthiness and return operands
program: [null ?? 1, 0 ?? 1, undefined ?? "d", 0 || 1, "" && 2, "a" && 2, null || undefined]

description: ?. short-circuits member, index and call on null/undefined
% takes the sign of the dividend
relational operators compare numbers numerically and two strings lexicographically
bitwise operators work on signed 32-bit integers
prefix and postfix ++/-- return the new and old value
??= ||= &&= assign only when the condition holds
program: let a = null; a ??= 5; let b = 1; b &&= 7; let c = 0; c ||= 9; let d = 2; d ??= 8; [a, b, c, d]

description: in tests own and inherited property names on objects
comma operator evaluates left to right and yields the last
member and index access on nested literals
program: const o = {a: 1, b: [1, 2, {c: 3}]}; [o.b[2].c + o["a"], o.b.length]

description: shorthand props, computed keys and method shorthand
program: const k = "dyn"; const a = 1; const o = {a, [k]: 2, ["x" + 1]: 3, add(p, q) { return p + q }}; [o.a, o.dyn, o.x1, o.add(2, 3)]

description: if / else if / else chain
program: let r; if (1 > 2) { r = "no" } else if (2 > 1) { r = "yes" } else { r = "?" } r

description: conditional operator
program: const v = 5; [v > 3 ? "big" : "small", v > 9 ? "big" : v > 4 ? "mid" : "small"]

description: classic for with continue
program: let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if (i === 3) continue; s += i } s

description: for-of with break over an array
program: let s = 0; for (const x of [1,2,3,4]) { if (x > 2) break; s += x } s

description: for-of iterates a string by character
program: const out = []; for (const ch of "abc") out.push(ch); out

description: for-in yields keys as strings, including array indices
program: const ks = []; for (const k in {a: 1, b: 2}) ks.push(k); const is = []; for (const i in [5, 6]) is.push(i); [ks, is]

description: while checks first, do-while runs once
program: let n = 0; while (n < 10) n += 3; let m = 0; do { m++ } while (m < 0); [n, m]

description: break leaves only the innermost loop
program: let n = 0; for (const a of [1, 2]) { for (const b of [1, 2, 3]) { if (b === 2) break; n++ } } n

description: closures keep their own mutable state
program: function mk() { let c = 0; return () => ++c } const f = mk(); const g = mk(); f(); f(); [f(), g()]

description: let in a for loop is bound per iteration
program: const fs = []; for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) fs.push(() => i); fs.map(f => f())

description: function declarations are hoisted
program: const r = twice(4); function twice(x) { return x * 2 } r

description: inner let shadows without touching the outer binding
program: let x = 1; const r = []; { let x = 2; r.push(x) } r.push(x); r

description: defaults apply for undefined only, can read earlier params
program: function f(a, b = a * 2) { return b } [f(4), f(1, undefined), f(1, null), f(1, 0)]

description: rest collects remaining arguments
program: function f(a, ...r) { return [a, r] } [f(1), f(1, 2, 3)]

description: expression-bodied, block-bodied and object-returning arrows
program: const a = x => x + 1; const b = (x, y) => { return x * y }; const c = () => ({k: 1}); [a(1), b(2, 3), c()]

description: IIFE and recursion
missing arguments are undefined, extra arguments ignored
program: function f(a, b) { return [a, b === undefined] } [f(1), f(1, 2, 3)]

description: object destructuring: rename, nested default, rest
program: const {a, b: {c = 5} = {}, ...rest} = {a: 1, x: 2, y: 3}; [a, c, rest]

description: array destructuring: holes, defaults, rest
program: const [p, , q = 9, ...r] = [7, 8, undefined, 1, 2]; [p, q, r]

description: destructuring in parameters
destructuring in for-of heads
program: let s = 0; for (const [k, v] of Object.entries({a: 1, b: 2})) s += v + k.length; s

description: swap via array destructuring assignment
spread in arrays, objects and calls; later keys win
try/catch/finally run in order
program: const log = []; try { log.push("t"); throw Error("boom") } catch (e) { log.push(e.message) } finally { log.push("f") } log

description: a return in finally overrides the try return
program: function f() { try { return 1 } finally { return 2 } } f()

description: finally runs even when try returns
program: const log = []; function f() { try { return 1 } finally { log.push('f') } } [f(), log]

description: any value can be thrown and caught
program: let v; try { throw {code: 7} } catch (e) { v = e.code } v

description: a rethrown error reaches the outer catch
program: let m; try { try { throw Error("inner") } catch (e) { throw Error("re:" + e.message) } } catch (e) { m = e.message } m

description: catch without a binding is legal
program: let r = "a"; try { throw 1 } catch { r = "b" } r

description: runtime faults are catchable TypeErrors
program: const out = []; try { null.x } catch (e) { out.push(e.name) } try { undefined() } catch (e) { out.push(e.name) } out

description: an uncaught throw fails the run with the message and line
program:
const a = 1
throw Error("kaput")
